title: Brother 1.0.20 night run manifest
description: ORCH-01. The IMMUTABLE run manifest a night run is launched from. This record holds NO volatile state: no task list, no current epoch, no progress. Those live in the journal (orchestrator-event-v1) and the task records (orchestrator-task-v1); a manifest that grew a mutable field would let a running orchestrator quietly rewrite the terms it was launched under. scripts/orchestrator_protocol.py enforces this file generically over type, required, properties, enum, const, additionalProperties, items, minItems, minimum and pattern; hard_stop_jst is checked against this schema's own pattern rather than a second copy of the clock format living in code.

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

run_id.description: Stable identifier for this one night run.

goal.description: The north star this run serves, plain language.

canonical_repo.description: The repository of record this run integrates into, never a lane's own worktree.

base_revision.description: The canonical revision this run started from.

hard_stop_jst.description: 24 hour clock, JST, HH:MM. Never defaulted from an assumed value: a manifest with no hard stop is refused outright, not read as never-stop.

orchestrators.description: The orchestrator identities authorized to run this manifest. At least one, so a run can never launch with nobody named to hold it.

builder_cap_policy.description: Name of the policy that turns machine and account limits into a live builder cap, for example a fixed cap or a load-adaptive one. The number itself is default_builder_cap; this names how it may be revised.

default_builder_cap.description: The starting cap on concurrent builders, before builder_cap_policy adjusts it.

integration_cap.description: Exactly one integrator at a time, always. Not a policy knob: a manifest naming any other value is malformed, because two integrators writing canonical truth at once is the exact defect this run exists to prevent.

max_outer_attempts.description: How many outer attempts a unit gets before it is parked rather than retried again.

max_same_strategy_attempts.description: How many times the same strategy may be retried unchanged before the run must try something else or stop.

red_actions.description: What happens to an action classified RED (irreversible, credentialed, or otherwise founder-only): it is refused and queued for the founder, never taken automatically. Fixed by law, not a per-run choice.

mandatory_evidence.description: Whether every unit in this run must clear its evidence_obligation before being read as done. False here does not lower any single unit's own evidence_obligation; it only says this run adds no blanket requirement beyond what each unit already carries.

cross_review_risk_classes.description: Which risk classes require a second, independent reviewer before merge in this run. An empty array means this run names none beyond what each task's own review_profile already requires.
